Definition: from G71; properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety:--conflict, contention, fight, race.
BiblicalUsage: Agon is a contest — a fight, a race, a struggle. Paul says the Philippians share the same conflict he has; he tells the Colossians of the great conflict he has for them; he charges Timothy to fight the good fight of faith; and Hebrews pictures the Christian life as a race, run with patience, with a cloud of witnesses watching. The word holds the whole Christian life in one picture: a contest worth entering, and worth finishing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word will not let the Christian life go soft. Faith is a fight and a race, not a stroll — and the same Paul who fought it tells me to lay hold on eternal life, to run with patience, and to look to Jesus, who ran it first and finished it.
